productIntro.text: Two printed images sit inside one physical frame - along with a tiny clock mechanism, a bit of thread, a trap door, and a falling weight. When the time is up, the frame reveals the hidden image.

detailGroups.heading: Wait, why?
detailGroups.body:
Halloween. April Fools. Baby reveals. Pet nonsense. Family holiday cards. Promposals.

Sincere messages of hope and inspiration, if you must insist.

Imagine giving someone a framed photo, letting it sit quietly on a shelf, and then - days or weeks later - they notice it's become a completely different picture.

detailGroups.heading: So it's both absurd and pointless. How do I get one?
detailGroups.body:
You build it! Download the ready-to-print files, print the parts, and put everything together. No modeling or design work required.

If you don't own a 3D printer, ask around - a friend, local library, or makerspace may have one. You can source the remaining hardware and materials yourself or get everything together in our Hardware Bundle.

detailGroups.heading: This whole 3D-printing craze doesn't interest me.
detailGroups.body: Fair enough. We'll print every plastic part and send it with the hardware and materials. You do the assembly. That's the Assembly Kit.

detailGroups.heading: Take the hint. I want a fun prank gift, not a project.
detailGroups.body: You're missing out! But if you insist, we'll sell you the Finished Gift - built, loaded, tested, and ready to give. It'll cost ya.

detailGroups.heading: How exactly does it work?
detailGroups.body: Simple: a clock winds a string, which pulls a zipper, which releases a latch, which drops a weight, which yoinks a photo, which reveals another.

detailGroups.heading: Will I enjoy putting this together?
detailGroups.body:
That depends almost entirely on what kind of project you enjoy.

This is a miniature machine disguised as a gift: part assembly project, part puzzle, and part experiment. If you enjoy examining unfamiliar parts, understanding how they interact, and making small adjustments until a mechanism comes to life, it is probably your kind of fun.

No individual step is especially difficult. But if you want a quick, strictly linear project that never asks you to stop and think, it may be more aggravating than enjoyable. The build rewards curiosity, patience, and a willingness to tinker.

detailGroups.heading: Is it fragile?
detailGroups.body: Not especially. Once it is set up, the mechanism can handle normal jostling, packing, shipping, and being tilted around. It does not need to stay upright the whole time. Just return it upright before the timer finishes so gravity can do its job.

detailGroups.heading: Can I choose one of the image pairs in the gallery?
detailGroups.body: Yes, but we would rather see what you come up with.

detailGroups.heading: Can I use any type of photo or paper stock?
detailGroups.body:
The sliding cover image requires the specified specialty paper.

The hidden image can use just about any roughly 5x7 photo or paper stock.

detailGroups.heading: Won't it seem weird to give someone a photo in this frame?
detailGroups.body: Probably. A cover story helps. Try: "My friend started 3D-printing frames and gave me one."

detailGroups.heading: Does it make noise?
detailGroups.body:
A little. The clock mechanism ticks softly, but unless your recipient is already inspecting the frame for tiny hidden machinery, they are unlikely to notice.

The reveal makes a small thud when the weight drops. A small piece of fabric or felt at the bottom helps muffle it.

assembly.intro: Before following the steps, it helps to understand the little chain reaction inside the frame. The instructions will walk you through the setup, but the mechanism is forgiving. Once you understand what each part is trying to do, you can use the steps as both a guide and a checklist.

sequenceItems.text: Clock mechanism sits inside the frame.
Capstan presses onto the clock mechanism.
Then runs through the clock/string guide hole.
Then ties to the zipper anchor.
Weight is tethered to the sliding cover image.
Cover image sits over the reveal image.
When the timer runs, the clock winds the string, pulls the zipper, releases the latch, drops the weight, slides the cover image up, and reveals the image underneath.

checklistItems: Tuck the stem of the weight inside the roller lip so it cannot fall out.
Fasten the trap-door latch with the C-clip.
Thread the string through both the clock/string guide hole and the top-left eyelet.
Pull any remaining slack above the string/clock guide.

items.question: How do I reset the mechanism?
items.answer: Return to the assembly instructions and repeat the steps that set the mechanism in motion. You will need to redo some of the assembly process, but not all of it.

items.question: Threading the string is a nuisance.
items.answer: It can be. Stiffen the end with a small drop of superglue, or glue the tiny metal wire included in the kit to the end of the string and use it as a threading needle.

items.question: I'm worried I assembled it incorrectly and it won't work.
items.answer: The design and assembly instructions include multiple layers of redundancy. Most individual steps are not essential on their own; instead, they work together to reduce the overall likelihood of failure to below 1%. If you get one detail slightly wrong, the mechanism will usually still work - you have most likely increased the risk of failure only marginally.

items.question: You've spoiled the surprise by writing the URL into the frame!
items.answer: Don't worry. It's hidden by the frame stand. They won't see it until they take it apart.

items.product: KOALA Waterproof Matte White Tear-Resistant Printable Vinyl Paper, 8.5 x 11 in.
items.note: Required. Used to print the Display Image.

items.product: PPD Double-Sided Photo Paper / Glossy Brochure Paper, 8.5 x 11 in., 140 gsm, 6.2 mil, instant-dry and water-resistant.
items.note: Recommended. Used to print the Reveal Image.

items.product: Clear, flexible PET sheet, 1 mm thick. Start with an 8 x 10 in. sheet and cut it to approximately 5.75 x 6.75 in.
items.note: Required. Use clear, flexible PET rather than rigid acrylic.

items.product: Backing-board sheet, 8 x 10 in. and approximately 1/20 in. thick. Cut to approximately 6.875 x 10 in.
items.note: Required. Use 6.875 in. for the cut dimension.

items.product: Reference movement - Young Town 12888SA. Threadless / snap-in 12888-style quartz clock movement, approximately 8 mm total shaft, step/ticking movement.
items.note: Required. Capstans are fitted to the reference movement; if you use a different brand/model, you will have to adjust the bore sizes of the capstans.
Recommended. Must unzip with very little resistance; reject any zipper that feels stiff or catches.
Required. Used as the clock-driven pull line.

items.quantity: Enough to fill the printed weight carriage
items.note: Recommended. Use small weights that can pack tightly into the carriage.
